overview: Studying Physiotherapy (MBBS Abroad) in Finland offers Indian students access to world-renowned Nordic education, innovative practical research, English-taught programmes, and excellent European career pathways.

faq.question: Can Indian students study Physiotherapy in Finland?
faq.answer: Yes, **Indian students can apply** to eligible Physiotherapy programmes in Finland, provided they meet the academic (Class 12), English language (B2 level), and programme-specific admission criteria.

faq.question: Is Physiotherapy taught in English in Finland?
faq.answer: Yes, international Physiotherapy programmes in Finland are available in English. For example, **Metropolia UAS** offers an international Bachelor of Physiotherapy that begins in English and progressively incorporates Finnish into clinical studies.

faq.question: How long is a Bachelor of Physiotherapy in Finland?
faq.answer: The international Bachelor of Physiotherapy at Metropolia consists of **210 ECTS credits** and takes approximately **3.5 years** of full-time study to complete.

faq.question: What is the tuition fee for Physiotherapy in Finland?
faq.answer: Tuition varies by institution. At Metropolia, the international Physiotherapy programme lists **€11,000 to €11,500 per academic year** for non-EU/EEA degree students. Partial performance scholarships may be available.

faq.question: Can I work as a physiotherapist in Finland after graduation?
faq.answer: Yes. After completing the recognised Finnish Physiotherapy qualification and obtaining professional authorisation from **Valvira**, graduates can practice as registered physiotherapists. Developing **Finnish language proficiency** is vital for clinical employment.
